title: Route all captures through mandatory guard; enforce invariants at bottlenecks
context: hunch_record_decision and hunch_record_correction bypassed putCapture by calling putPrivate/json.put directly. putCapture's contract (all paths funnel through it) documents a cross-home twin guard, but bypassing it allowed one id to exist in both memory homes, creating duplicate live decisions on one topic with silent downstream failures. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Establish putCapture as a mandatory routing bottleneck for all record writes. Remove selective per-home writer calls; all captures now flow through putCapture, which enforces the twin-prevention guard. Convert guard throws to clean tool errors instead of silent failures.
consequences: Eliminates silent data corruption where twins could coexist across stores
Makes invariant violations fail loudly and traceable, not silently
Establishes documented guards as non-negotiable, not optional optimizations
Requires future callers to respect centralized function contracts
alternatives_rejected: Inline the guard logic into each per-home writer (scatters invariant, harder to audit)
Remove/weaken the guard to allow twins (violates uniqueness, breaks downstream logic)
Document the bypass as 'safe' and leave it (pushes guard reasoning onto every caller)
